source_review.notes: Checked IEC 61078:2016 and current IEC TC 56 status; NASA-STD-8729.1A, current NASA reliability/maintainability resources, KSC preferred practices and Lesson 825; NASA tri-agency mission-extension guidance and Systems Engineering Handbook; and NIST survival/complex-system formulas. All ten final URLs returned HTTP 200. Claims distinguish normative requirements, agency practices, statistical identities and the chapter's engineering synthesis.

evidence: Reviewed binary success structure, coherence and series/parallel reliability expressions.
Reviewed identical-independent k-out-of-n binomial expression and its scope.
Reviewed exponential lifetime and additive series-hazard relation.
Reviewed exact independent-state enumeration, minimal path/cut and hazard notation.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Reliability, failure probability/rate/frequency, availability and maintainability are consistently distinguished.

evidence: Executed rbd-series-parallel-fixture under python3 with exact output recorded in artifacts/snippets/SYSENG-063/report.json.
Enumerated all sixteen states and confirmed their probabilities sum to 1.00000000.
Recomputed sensor parallel reliability 0.99960000 and system reliability 0.95991588.
Recomputed single-sensor reliability 0.94109400 and modeled gain 0.01882188.
Recomputed worked series 0.941094, parallel-with-bus 0.97755, 2-of-3 0.998816, exponential 0.98020 and exercise values 0.921888/0.95876352/0.972.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Arithmetic assumes declared independent, capacity-sufficient success events and does not validate block data or real architecture.

evidence: Confirmed the fixture structure is (sensor_a OR sensor_b) AND controller AND actuator.
Confirmed two minimal paths and three minimal cuts by logical duality and direct inspection.
Confirmed structure monotonicity over every componentwise-comparable enumerated state.
Confirmed series and parallel formulas derive from intersection and complement under independence.
Confirmed exact enumeration requires a joint distribution when component states are dependent.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Static coherent identities are not applied to standby, repair, sequence or noncoherent systems without a suitable model.

evidence: Challenged physical-schematic substitution, vague success, mixed mission phases, degraded capacity and incompatible paths.
Reviewed series, parallel, unequal/identical k-of-n, bridge, noncoherent and dynamic structures.
Reviewed active/standby, dormancy, detection, isolation, switching, delay, load sharing and repair semantics.
Reviewed shared design/software/power/environment/process/maintenance/operator, CCF and double counting.
Reviewed constant-rate, demand/cycle/wear-out/systematic failure, units/time bases, censoring and sparse demonstrations.
Reviewed solver identity/reduction/enumeration/BDD/simulation, truncation, convergence and limiting cases.
Reviewed importance/allocation misuse, uncertainty, redundancy-created modes and lifecycle configuration changes.
Reviewed all ten examples and five complete answers for assumptions, reasoning, limitations and bounded conclusions.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Production RBDA still requires domain, reliability/statistical, software/human, maintainability/logistics, common-cause, test, configuration, tool and decision-authority review appropriate to consequence.

evidence: Confirmed function, threshold, mission/time, configuration/environment and repair credit precede modeling.
Confirmed functional success connectivity remains distinct from physical topology.
Confirmed shared dependencies and coverage are explicit rather than hidden by parallel boxes.
Confirmed block data retain distribution, units, population, provenance, uncertainty and applicability.
Confirmed structural, dependency, stochastic, computational, empirical and decision validity remain separate gates.
Confirmed model updates retain historical baselines and no prediction is labeled demonstrated reliability.
invariant_checking.notes: Nominal redundancy and calculated precision never substitute for independence, capacity, evidence or acceptance.

proof_review.notes: The chapter derives standard reliability identities but presents no theorem proof.

proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No passage is presented as a proof sketch.

evidence: The fixture labels evidence synthetic_independent_events_only and lists excluded phenomena.
IEC edition/stability and NASA/NIST publication status are attributed.
Every quantitative example names independence, mission, lifetime or capacity assumptions.
Zero-failure demonstration is explicitly an upper-bound example rather than proof of reliability one.
No external review, real-system reliability, independence, common-cause completeness, safety or design acceptance is claimed.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Predictions and demonstrations are treated as distinct bounded evidence.

conceptual_review.notes: Internal conceptual review checked reliability, RBD/block, series/parallel/k-of-n, active/standby redundancy, minimal paths/cuts, coherence, mission reliability versus availability, common cause, coverage and importance.

practitioner_review.notes: Internal practitioner-oriented review checked success definition, functional modeling, capacity, redundancy, lifetime/time bases, repair, paths/cuts, bridge networks, dependencies, double counting, importance, allocation, uncertainty, structural/tool/empirical validation, action and lifecycle maintenance.

pedagogical_review.notes: Internal pedagogical review confirmed progression from success-space semantics through closed forms, complex/dynamic cases, evidence and decision use. Ten examples isolate recurring errors; five complete solutions cover shared-dependency construction, series-parallel arithmetic, voting, standby and lifecycle validation.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external IEC/NASA/NIST expert, reliability statistician, domain architect, software/human-reliability specialist, operator/maintainer/logistics owner, common-cause analyst, test/demonstration authority, solver vendor, independent V&V, safety, certification, technical-authority or design-acceptance review is claimed.
